Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Pinnacle Asset Management Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Pinnacle Asset Management's Q2 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Investment Officer; David Chen, Head of Distribution; and Lisa Patel, Head of Operations.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q2. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by innovative new product launches and outstanding fund performance rankings. Our AUM grew to $1.28 trillion.

Thank you for that comprehensive overview from our financial team in advance, but now I'd like to turn to one of our key growth drivers: our new product launches and the continued strength in fund performance rankings, particularly as reflected in Morningstar ratings. In the asset management industry, innovation and consistent outperformance are table stakes for capturing wallet share from both institutional and retail clients. We're not just keeping pace with leaders like BlackRock and Vanguard; we're setting the bar higher with targeted launches and alpha generation that resonates in this environment of moderating inflation, potential Fed rate cuts, and heightened geopolitical volatility.

Let me start with new product launches, where we've seen robust momentum. In the first quarter leading into Q2, we successfully rolled out three flagship strategies, generating over $4.2 billion in net new inflows within the first 90 days—a 25% beat on our internal targets. This represents our strongest quarterly launch performance since the 2021 alternatives boom.

First, our Pinnacle Sustainable Global Equity ETF (ticker: PSEF), launched on January 15th. This actively managed ETF targets companies with strong ESG credentials while delivering competitive risk-adjusted returns. We've embedded proprietary climate risk modeling using satellite data and AI-driven scenario analysis to quantify transition risks under both IEA's Net Zero by 2050 and Stated Policies scenarios. Early results are promising: PSEF has already amassed $1.8 billion in AUM, with 60% of inflows from European institutional clients via UCITS wrappers, capitalizing on the EU's SFDR Article 8 and 9 classifications. Retail adoption has been equally strong in the US, where we've seen 35% subscription growth week-over-week on platforms like Schwab and Fidelity, driven by millennial and Gen Z investors allocating to sustainable themes amid record heatwaves and COP28 commitments.

Complementing this, we introduced the Pinnacle Private Credit Opportunities Fund (PCOF) on February 1st, a semi-liquid interval fund targeting middle-market direct lending in the US and select APAC markets. With base rates still elevated around SOFR + 450bps, we're yielding north of 11% net of fees, with a weighted average LTV of 55% and minimal covenant-lite exposure. This launch tapped into the $1.7 trillion private credit universe—growing at 15% CAGR per Preqin data—and drew $1.5 billion from high-net-worth individuals and family offices wary of public high-yield spreads compressing to 350bps. Regionally, 40% of commitments came from Asia-Pacific sovereign wealth funds, reflecting their pivot from core fixed income amid China's property sector deleveraging.

Finally, addressing the retirement savings megatrend, we unveiled the Pinnacle Target 2050 Retirement Series on March 1st, a suite of five target-date funds incorporating glide path optimization via Monte Carlo simulations and liability-driven investing principles. These funds blend 60/40 equities-fixed income with a 20% allocation to alternatives, dynamically shifting based on longevity risk and inflation forecasts from our macroeconomic nowcasting models. Initial AUM stands at $900 million, with 70% from defined contribution plans via partnerships with Empower and Prudential, positioning us to capture share in the $10 trillion US DC market as auto-enrollment mandates expand under SECURE 2.0.

These launches aren't siloed; they're part of our broader NextGen Platform, a cloud-native tech stack built on Snowflake and Palantir Foundry, enabling real-time portfolio construction, stress testing under 10,000 Fed dot plot scenarios, and seamless integration with Aladdin-like risk analytics. This has reduced time-to-market for new products by 40% and boosted operational alpha through lower tracking error—now averaging 0.8% versus the industry 1.5% per Morningstar direct data.

Shifting to fund performance rankings, our strategies continue to shine, underscoring the durability of our active management edge. As of March 31st, 78% of our rated equity funds hold Morningstar 4- or 5-star ratings over the 3-year period, up from 72% at year-end—a testament to our bottom-up stock selection and sector rotation amid the Magnificent Seven's dominance and regional rotations into value.

Take our cornerstone Pinnacle Large Cap Growth Fund (PLCG), a $28 billion behemoth with a 5-star Morningstar rating across 1-, 3-, and 5-year horizons. YTD through Q1 into Q2, it delivered 12.4% net returns, outpacing the S&P 500's 10.2% by 220bps, with a Sharpe ratio of 1.45 versus the benchmark's 1.12. This alpha stems from our overweight in AI infrastructure plays like NVIDIA and TSMC, balanced by defensive tilts into healthcare amid biotech M&A waves. Over 10 years, PLCG ranks in the top decile of its Lipper peer group, generating 2.1% annualized alpha net of fees.

In fixed income, our Pinnacle Core Bond Fund (PCBF) maintained its 5-star status, returning 2.8% YTD against the Bloomberg US Aggregate's 1.1%, thanks to our barbell strategy: 45% in short-duration investment-grade corporates (yielding 5.2%) and 25% in securitized products like CLOs at 7.5% blended. This has resonated in Europe, where PCBF's UCITS share class saw €500 million in inflows, outperforming 90% of eurozone peers per Morningstar EU ratings.

Internationally, the Pinnacle Emerging Markets Equity Fund (PEMEF) climbed to a 4-star rating, surging 8.5% YTD on India and Mexico cyclicals, beating the MSCI EM Index's 5.2% by 330bps. We've tactically underweighted China to 18% from 25%, rotating into ASEAN consumer staples amid supply chain reshoring—a move that's added 150bps of attribution per our Barra risk model.

Regionally, APAC has been a standout: 65% of our top-quartile funds are domiciled there, with AUM growth of 22% YoY, fueled by inflows from Japan's GPIF and Korea's NPS seeking US small-cap exposure via our 5-star Pinnacle US Small Cap Value Fund (PUSHV), which returned 14.2% YTD versus Russell 2000's 4.8%. In EMEA, ESG mandates drove 30% organic growth in our sustainable suite, while US retail platforms contributed 45% of total inflows, with Robinhood and Vanguard integrations lifting our ETF market share to 1.2% in actives.

Strategically, these results affirm our conviction in multi-asset active management as the antidote to passive saturation—now 48% of US equity AUM per EPFR data. We're doubling down on alternatives, targeting $20 billion in private assets by 2025, and enhancing our quant capabilities with reinforcement learning for dynamic asset allocation. Amid sticky inflation and election risks, our funds' low beta (0.92 average) and high information ratios (0.65) position clients for resilient returns.

In summary, our new launches and stellar rankings aren't just numbers—they're proof of our ability to deliver on client mandates in a fragmented, fee-compressed world. We're proud to report record organic flows of $12.5 billion in Q1 spilling into Q2, with long-term AUM up 14% YoY to $1.28 trillion.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael Rivera.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Pinnacle Asset Management delivered strong results in Q2. Our revenue was $2.28 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by robust net flows totaling $25.4 billion for the quarter. 

Good afternoon, everyone. Before diving deeper into the segment results, I'd like to provide a detailed walkthrough of our net flows by channel—institutional, retail, and alternatives—which totaled that robust $25.4 billion for the quarter. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of positive net flows and represents a 15% sequential increase from Q1's $22.1 billion. Year-to-date, we're at $47.5 billion, putting us on track for our strongest full-year inflow performance since 2021, driven by our disciplined product positioning amid volatile markets.

Let me break this down channel by channel, with key trends, regional insights, and strategic context.

Institutional Channel: $15.2 billion in net inflows (60% of total). Our institutional business remains the bedrock of Pinnacle's flow story, delivering $15.2 billion in net new assets—up 22% quarter-over-quarter. This was propelled by strong mandates wins in liability-driven investing (LDI) strategies, particularly our custom fixed-income overlays for defined benefit pension plans, which captured $4.8 billion alone. Performance attribution here was stellar: our core-plus aggregate bond strategy outperformed its Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate benchmark by 45 basis points over three years, fueling reallocation from underperforming peers.

Regionally, North America accounted for 65% of inflows at $9.9 billion, with notable wins from U.S. corporate pensions shifting into our multi-asset credit solutions amid the inverted yield curve. EMEA contributed $3.7 billion, bolstered by sovereign wealth fund allocations to our infrastructure debt funds, while APAC added $1.6 billion—our fastest-growing institutional region—driven by Japanese GPIF-like pools favoring our yen-hedged equity sleeves.

Strategically, we've leaned into technical initiatives like our proprietary Aladdin-inspired risk analytics platform, which enabled model portfolio delivery for 20 new OCIO mandates totaling $2.5 billion. Looking ahead, we're positioning for Fed rate cuts by emphasizing short-duration, investment-grade credit with yields north of 5%, targeting $20 billion in H2 wins as defined contribution plans rotate from cash proxies.

Retail Channel: $5.1 billion in net inflows (20% of total). Retail flows came in at $5.1 billion, a solid rebound from Q1's $3.8 billion, reflecting improved equity sentiment post the S&P 500's 10% Q2 rally. ETF inflows dominated at $3.2 billion, led by our Pinnacle U.S. Large Cap Growth ETF (PGLG), which gathered $1.2 billion amid the AI thematic surge—now the #3 performer in its Morningstar category with $18 billion in AUM. Mutual fund flows added $1.4 billion, primarily in target-date funds for 401(k) rollovers, while separately managed accounts (SMAs) contributed $0.5 billion via our robo-advisor integration with platforms like Schwab and Fidelity.

Regionally, U.S. retail drove 72% or $3.7 billion, with wirehouse channels like Morgan Stanley seeing accelerated advisor adoption of our active semi-transparent ETFs. Europe lagged at $0.8 billion due to UCITS redemption pressures from high-beta equity outflows, but we're countering this with our new EMU-focused sustainable equity UCITS launch. APAC retail ticked up to $0.6 billion, fueled by retail platforms in Hong Kong and Singapore chasing our thematic SMID-cap strategies.

Key trends include a 12% quarter-over-quarter rise in organic retail growth rates, outpacing industry averages per EPFR data. Our tech edge—deploying API-driven direct indexing for tax-alpha optimization—has reduced beta slippage in SMAs to under 10 bps, winning share from Vanguard's low-cost behemoths. Forward-looking, with consumer confidence rebounding and potential rate relief, we're targeting $12 billion in H2 retail flows through active ETF conversions and advisor education on our 130/30 long-short equity suites.

Alternatives Channel: $5.1 billion in net inflows (20% of total). Alternatives rounded out the quarter with $5.1 billion in net inflows, flat sequentially but up 30% year-over-year, underscoring our premium-fee franchise resilience. Private credit led with $2.3 billion, including a $1.1 billion commitment to our evergreen direct lending fund from a Middle Eastern SWF, yielding mid-teens IRRs amid bank retrenchment under Basel III. Private equity added $1.5 billion, highlighted by second-close commitments to our mid-market buyout vehicle targeting U.S. software and industrials—now at $4.2 billion hard-close. Real assets, including infrastructure and real estate, contributed $1.3 billion, with European pension inflows into our renewable energy co-investments.

Regionally, EMEA was the standout at 45% or $2.3 billion, driven by UK LGPS pools allocating to our core-plus real estate amid office-to-residential repurposing trends. North America followed at $1.9 billion, while APAC's $0.9 billion reflected Singaporean family offices dipping into our Asia infrastructure debt amid Belt-and-Road unwind opportunities.

From a technical standpoint, our GP-led secondaries platform processed $800 million in Q2, offering liquidity solutions with 15-20% J-curve compression. Strategically, we're scaling our perpetual alternatives vehicle—launched last year—to $50 billion AUM by 2025, blending evergreen structures with GP stakes for yield-hungry insurers. Amid dry powder fatigue industry-wide (per Preqin data showing $2.5 trillion uncommitted), our focus on niche secondaries and transition capital positions us for outperformance as cap rates compress.

In summary on flows, these grew AUM to $1.28 trillion, with 85% organic growth excluding markets. Our channel diversification—60/20/20 mix—de-risks against retail volatility while capturing institutional stickiness and alts fee power.

Our expenses were $1.65 billion, resulting in net income of $600 million. Our expense ratio improved due to scale effects and technological advancements. Now, turning to our efficiency ratios, with a particular focus on our expense ratio, which remains a cornerstone of our competitive positioning in the asset management industry. As you know, in our business, efficiency isn't just about cutting costs—it's about leveraging scale, technology, and product mix to deliver superior net returns to clients while maintaining healthy operating margins. Our weighted average expense ratio stood at 21.5 basis points (bps) for Q2, down 8% year-over-year from 23.4 bps in Q2 2023, and marking our 11th consecutive quarter of sequential improvement.

For context, the expense ratio is calculated as our total operating expenses—excluding distribution and variable incentives—divided by average monthly AUM. This metric captures the true cost of managing client assets and is a key differentiator in an era of persistent fee compression. Industry-wide, according to Morningstar's latest data, the average expense ratio for U.S. equity mutual funds sits at around 52 bps, while ETFs average just 18 bps. We're proud to be in the vanguard of low-cost leadership, outperforming the ETF peer average by over 20% and aligning closely with Vanguard's benchmark of 19 bps across their passive suite.

Let me break this down by key drivers. First, scale effects from AUM growth were pivotal. Our AUM reached a record $1.28 trillion, up 14% year-over-year, driven by $45 billion in net inflows, particularly into our low-cost beta products like the Pinnacle S&P 500 ETF (PSP500), which now manages $180 billion at a rock-bottom 3 bps fee. This scale diluted fixed costs—think compliance, custody, and middle-office operations—by about 4 bps on a standalone basis.

Second, product mix optimization. Passive and ETF strategies, which now represent 68% of AUM (up from 62% last year), carry an average expense ratio of just 12 bps, compared to 38 bps for our active strategies. We've strategically shifted flows here amid client demand for cost efficiency, especially post the 2022 rate hikes when active managers underperformed benchmarks by 200-300 bps on average, per Lipper data. Our active quant funds, like the Pinnacle Global Alpha Fund, benefited from fee waivers that brought their ratio down to 45 bps without sacrificing alpha generation.

Regionally, performance varied tellingly. In the U.S., our core market at 72% of AUM, the expense ratio was 20 bps—bolstered by our Chicago HQ's proximity to CME futures markets, reducing trading costs by 15% via direct electronic access. Europe, at 15% of AUM, came in at 25 bps, reflecting MiFID II and PRIIPs regulatory overhead, but we've clawed back 5 bps through our Luxembourg hub's UCITS platform standardization. Notably, Asia-Pacific, now 10% of AUM after $12 billion in inflows from Hong Kong and Singapore mandates, achieved an impressive 18 bps—our lowest regional ratio—thanks to partnerships with local custodians like HSBC and DBS, which cut settlement costs amid the HKEX's T+1 shift.

Technical initiatives have been game-changers here. In Q1, we fully migrated our Aladdin-alternative portfolio management system to a hybrid cloud infrastructure with AWS and Google Cloud, slashing data processing costs by 22% and enabling real-time expense analytics. We've also rolled out AI-driven expense forecasting via our proprietary "Effex" tool, which uses machine learning on historical NAV data and flow projections to preemptively optimize fee waivers—saving an estimated $25 million annually. On the custody side, blockchain pilots with State Street's digital asset platform have reduced reconciliation times from T+2 to near-real-time for our $50 billion crypto-linked ETFs, trimming ops expenses by 10 bps.

Strategically, this efficiency underscores our "Scale-to-Win" framework amid broader industry headwinds. Fee pressure from ETF proliferation—BlackRock's iShares suite alone commands 35% U.S. market share—and regulatory scrutiny like the SEC's proposed T+1 settlement rules are intensifying. Yet, our operating expense ratio of 28% (versus the industry's 35%) positions us to capture share in high-growth areas like ESG and private markets. For instance, our Pinnacle Sustainable Global ETF (PSUSG) at 15 bps has attracted $8 billion YTD, blending low costs with green bond indexing tied to Bloomberg's MSCI ESG Leaders.

Looking ahead, we expect the full-year expense ratio to hit 21 bps, assuming mid-single-digit AUM growth and stable markets. Risks include FX volatility in EM exposures and potential active fee rebates if dispersion narrows further, but our cost discipline—capped at 2% OpEx growth—mitigates this. We're also exploring sub-10 bps "zero-fee" betas for mega-AUM products, à la Fidelity's ZERO funds, to defend against fintech disruptors like Robinhood's index offerings.

In summary, our efficiency ratios reflect disciplined execution, technological edge, and client-centric innovation—delivering $2.1 billion in cost savings passed through to investors last year alone. This not only boosts our 42% operating margin but fortifies long-term moats in a maturing industry.

As we review our results today, I'd like to dive deeply into our capital allocation strategy, which remains the cornerstone of delivering superior risk-adjusted returns for our shareholders while positioning us for sustained long-term growth in the asset management industry. Our approach is disciplined, opportunistic, and aligned with three core pillars: fueling organic AUM growth, enhancing operational efficiency through technology, and maximizing shareholder value. Let me break this down with specifics from the quarter and our forward-looking framework.

First, a quick recap of our capital deployment over the past 12 months. We generated $4.2 billion in free cash flow from operations, underpinned by 11% year-over-year fee-related revenue growth to $8.7 billion annually run-rate, driven by net new organic inflows of $85 billion—our strongest since 2021. Of this, approximately 65% was allocated to organic growth initiatives, 20% to technology and infrastructure, 10% to mergers and acquisitions, and the remaining 5% to direct shareholder returns via dividends. This mix has yielded a 14% ROIC on incremental capital deployed, outperforming our 12% cost of capital hurdle by a meaningful margin.

Pillar 1: Organic Growth and Product Innovation (65% Allocation). Our top priority continues to be scaling AUM through high-conviction product launches and seeding strategies, capitalizing on structural tailwinds like the great wealth transfer—estimated at $84 trillion over the next two decades—and the relentless shift toward passive and alternatives. In Q2, we deployed $1.8 billion in seed capital across 12 new strategies, including three active ETFs tracking thematic indices in AI infrastructure and clean energy transition, which have already attracted $450 million in third-party inflows within 90 days of launch.

We're particularly excited about our alternatives platform, where AUM grew 28% YoY to $220 billion, outpacing the industry average of 18% per Preqin data. This includes $750 million seeded into our new evergreen private credit fund, targeting mid-market direct lending yields of LIBOR + 550 bps, with a focus on resilient sectors like healthcare and software-as-a-service. Regionally, North America remains our bedrock at 58% of total AUM ($1.45 trillion adjusted base), but we're accelerating in APAC, where we allocated $500 million to localize our ETF suite for the Hong Kong Stock Connect and Shanghai-Shenzhen exchanges. APAC AUM surged 22% YoY to $210 billion, fueled by 15% net inflows into our low-cost index funds amid China's gradual market liberalization. In EMEA, ESG mandates drove 32% growth in sustainable strategies to $180 billion, with our EU SFDR Article 8 and 9 funds capturing $12 billion in institutional mandates from Nordic pensions.

Pillar 2: Technology and Infrastructure Investments (20% Allocation). In an era of fee compression—where average ETF fees have fallen to 18 bps from 25 bps five years ago—we're investing aggressively to drive structural cost savings and alpha generation. We committed $850 million this year to our next-gen platform, 'Pinnacle AlphaEngine,' building on proprietary quant models akin to BlackRock's Aladdin but with enhanced AI-driven risk analytics and natural language processing for sentiment analysis across 50,000 global securities. This initiative is already delivering: our tech-enabled active equity strategies outperformed benchmarks by 220 bps over the trailing three years, contributing to a 15% reduction in our G&A expense ratio to 22% of revenues.

Regionally, we're tailoring these tools for emerging markets volatility; for instance, machine learning overlays on our LatAm fixed income funds have improved Sharpe ratios by 0.3 amid EM currency swings. Looking ahead, we expect these investments to generate $300 million in annualized expense synergies by 2026, with a payback period under 18 months.

Pillar 3: M&A and Shareholder Returns (15% Allocation). Discipline here is paramount—we only pursue deals that are immediately accretive to EPS and expand our moat. In Q1 into Q2, we closed the $1.2 billion acquisition of a key alternatives manager, adding $95 billion in alternatives AUM at a 7x fee-related earnings multiple, well below our historical average of 11x. This bolsters our private markets capabilities, similar to how TPG has scaled via bolt-ons, and is expected to add $150 million in recurring revenues by FY25. We've earmarked $2.5 billion for tuck-in M&A over the next 24 months, targeting boutique RIAs in high-growth niches like model portfolios and direct indexing.

I'll now turn to our mergers and acquisitions activity, which continues to be a cornerstone of our inorganic growth strategy at Pinnacle Asset Management. As many of you know, the asset management industry is undergoing accelerated consolidation amid persistent fee compression—now averaging 25-30 basis points on passive strategies versus 60-80 bps on active—and the relentless shift toward scale to compete with behemoths like BlackRock and Vanguard. With global AUM surpassing $120 trillion, per Morningstar data, we're laser-focused on bolt-on acquisitions that enhance our product diversification, geographic footprint, and technological edge, particularly in high-margin alternatives and ETFs.

Let me start with our flagship deal closed in Q2: the $1.4 billion acquisition of Pinnacle Alternatives Group, a leading U.S.-based manager of evergreen private credit and real assets strategies. Pinnacle Alternatives brought $32 billion in AUM at close, with a blended fee rate of 85 basis points, predominantly from direct lending and infrastructure debt funds. This transaction was immediately accretive, contributing $115 million in annualized revenue run-rate and boosting our alternatives platform to over $180 billion in AUM—a 22% year-over-year increase. Synergies are tracking ahead of our $45 million target for Year 1, driven by cross-selling our institutional client base—think CalPERS and OMERS analogs—into Pinnacle Alternatives' high-yield strategies, which have delivered a 12% net IRR over the past five years amid rising rates.

Integration has been seamless, leveraging our proprietary SynergyForge platform, a cloud-based operating system built on Snowflake and Palantir tech stacks, which has accelerated Pinnacle Alternatives' funds onto our rails in under 90 days—versus the industry average of 180. We've already realized 60% of cost synergies through vendor consolidation and headcount optimization, reducing the combined G&A ratio from 28% to 22%. Looking ahead, we're deploying AI-driven portfolio optimization tools from our quant team to enhance Pinnacle Alternatives' credit selection models, targeting a 200 bps uplift in risk-adjusted returns.

Regionally, this builds on our European expansion via the Q4 2023 merger with a Dublin-domiciled ETF provider with €18 billion in UCITS-compliant ETFs focused on thematic ESG and smart beta. That deal, valued at €650 million, has driven 35% organic inflows YTD, outpacing the €1.2 trillion European ETF market's 12% growth, per ETFGI. Post-merger, our EU AUM now exceeds €50 billion, positioning us to capture the MiFID II-driven demand for low-cost, transparent vehicles amid the UCITS wrapper's 15% AUM CAGR.

In APAC, where we've seen $2.5 trillion in net new money over the past two years per Cerulli Associates, we're advancing a tuck-in acquisition of a Singapore-based robo-advisor platform for SGD 420 million. This adds 150,000 high-net-worth clients and $8 billion in discretionary AUM, with tech that integrates seamlessly into our Aladdin-like risk management system. It's a bet on digital wrappers amid China's wealth transfer boom—projected at RMB 84 trillion by 2030—and positions us against local players while complying with MAS licensing.

Strategically, these moves align with our "Scale + Specialization" thesis: M&A now accounts for 40% of our AUM growth, up from 25% in 2022, allowing us to defend our 42 bps blended fee rate against Vanguard's 8 bps passive onslaught. We've also fortified our talent pipeline, onboarding 120 specialists from these deals, including top-quartile PMs in privates. Risks? Integration execution and regulatory hurdles like Hart-Scott-Rodino reviews, but our track record—95% on-time closes over five deals—mitigates that.

Our M&A pipeline remains robust at $5-7 billion in deployable capital, targeting 3-5 deals annually in boutiques with >15% EBITDA margins and sticky institutional mandates. We're prioritizing real assets for inflation hedging, given 7-10% expected U.S. CPI persistence, and active fixed income amid Fed pivot uncertainties.

On shareholder returns, we've returned $1.9 billion YTD through $1.4 billion in share repurchases—reducing shares outstanding by 3.2%—and a $0.85 quarterly dividend, yielding 2.8% at current prices. We've authorized an additional $3 billion buyback, opportunistic given our P/E of 15x versus the industry at 17x. Post-repurchase, we project EPS growth of 13% in 2025, assuming 8-10% AUM growth.

Strategic Insights and Outlook. Our allocation framework is dynamic, stress-tested quarterly against scenarios like a 100 bps Fed rate cut cycle or prolonged equity derating. Key trends informing this: ETF AUM industry-wide hit $12 trillion globally, with passives now 48% of total assets per Morningstar; we're targeting 20% share of that pie via our 450+ ETF lineup. In alternatives, dry powder sits at $3.7 trillion (per McKinsey), and we're positioning with GP stakes and co-investments. Risks include regulatory headwinds like the SEC's swing pricing rules or EU PRIIPs restrictions, but our diversified footprint—60% US, 20% EMEA, 15% APAC, 5% LatAm/EM—mitigates this.

In summary, this strategy has driven 16% total shareholder return over three years, beating the MSCI World Index by 400 bps. We're confident it will sustain 12-15% EPS CAGR through the decade.

Before we open the line for Q&A, I'll provide our forward-looking guidance for Q3 and full-year 2024, grounded in our current AUM trajectory, net flow momentum, market assumptions, and disciplined expense management. As always, our guidance incorporates a base case of moderate global equity returns of 4-6% annualized in Q3, with fixed income yields stabilizing around 4.2-4.5% amid Fed pauses, and continued ETF net inflows of $150-200 billion industry-wide, per EPFR data.

Revenue Guidance: $2.45-$2.55 Billion for Q3; $10.2-$10.5 Billion Full-Year (8-11% YoY Growth).

Starting with revenues, we expect Q3 revenues of $2.45 to $2.55 billion, representing 9-13% sequential growth from Q2's $2.28 billion and 8-11% full-year growth at the midpoint. This reflects robust AUM expansion to $1.32-$1.36 trillion by quarter-end, up from $1.28 trillion today, driven by 5-7% organic growth from markets and $25-$30 billion in quarterly net inflows.

Breaking it down by revenue stream:

- Management and Advisory Fees (85% of Revenues): $2.10-$2.18 billion in Q3, or 85-86% of total. Average fee rates hold steady at 42-43 bps, with modest compression to 41 bps full-year from passive ETF mix-shift, mirroring BlackRock's iShares trajectory. AUM growth is led by equities at +8% QoQ (S&P 500 base case +5%), multi-asset solutions +6%, and fixed income +4%, bolstered by our Pinnacle Core Bond ETF, which has captured 15% market share in intermediate-duration IG credits amid yield curve steepening.

- Performance Fees (8% of Revenues): $180-$220 million, up 20-30% QoY from realized carry in alternatives. Our private credit and infrastructure pools—$85 billion AUM, including the Pinnacle Infra Partners fund—are on track for $400 million full-year realizations, assuming 12-15% IRRs, ahead of pace due to refinancing activity in energy transition deals.

- Distribution and Service Fees (5% of Revenues): $120-$130 million, flat QoQ, supported by our retirement channel partnerships with firms like Fidelity and Schwab, where 401(k) DC plan assets grew 12% YoY to $150 billion.

- Other Income (2% of Revenues): $40-$50 million, including tech platform licensing from our Pinnacle Digital Wealth suite, now servicing 2.5 million RIAs with AI-driven model portfolios.

Key Trends and Strategic Drivers:

Regionally, North America remains our anchor at 65% of AUM ($830 billion), with U.S. ETF flows accelerating to $18-$22 billion quarterly, fueled by our low-cost Pinnacle S&P 500 ETF (0.03% TER), which has outperformed Vanguard's VOO on tracking error. EMEA (20% of AUM, $260 billion) sees tempered +3% growth due to UCITS outflows from active equity, but offset by +10% in sustainable strategies—our Pinnacle ESG Global Equity fund hit €15 billion AUM post-regulatory tailwinds from SFDR Level 2 disclosures. APAC (12% of AUM, $155 billion) is the growth engine at +9% QoQ, with onshore China inflows into our QDII products amid CSI 300 stabilization, and Japan retail via NISA accounts adding $5 billion.

Strategically, we're leaning into operating leverage from scale: net flows target $110-$120 billion full-year (4% of average AUM), with 60% retail/wealth, 25% institutional, and 15% alternatives. Initiatives like our GenAI Portfolio Optimizer—rolled out Q1—have boosted active ETF retention by 15% via dynamic alpha overlays, while our blockchain-enabled fund admin tech reduces NAV reconciliation times by 40%, positioning us against fintech disruptors like State Street's Alpha platform.

Expense Guidance: $1.65-$1.70 Billion for Q3; $6.9-$7.1 Billion Full-Year (2-4% YoY Growth; Expense-to-Revenue Ratio 66-68%).

On expenses, we guide to $1.65-$1.70 billion in Q3 (flat to +2% sequential) and $6.9-$7.1 billion full-year, implying just 2-4% growth versus 8-11% revenue expansion. This delivers adjusted operating margin expansion to 28-30% full-year (from 26% in 2023), with EBITDA of $3.4-$3.6 billion.

By category:
